entries.clue: Cast takes on a hunt (6)

indicatorNotes.takes on: to take something on is to take it in, so FORGE holds the A

blocks.note: to cast metal is to forge it

annotation.surface: A theatre company signs up for a hunt, perhaps a treasure hunt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' wants to be the actors; here it is the verb from metalwork. The A slips in after FOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: animals search for food by rummaging about, and the noun works the same way, a forage being a hunt.

entries.clue: Italian director collapsed in current (7)

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A film director collapses into a river or the flow of electricity.
annotation.walkthrough: Federico Fellini made La Dolce Vita. I for current comes from physics formulae.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the maker of La Dolce Vita and 8½ is one of the best-known filmmakers Italy produced.

entries.clue: Sauces made using spun sugar (5)

indicatorNotes.spun: spun letters are whirled into a new order

annotation.surface: A cook makes sauces from spun sugar, as for candyfloss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spun sugar' is a real confectioner's term, which hides the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the slow-cooked Bolognese meat sauce is one kind of sauce, pluralised to match.

entries.clue: Speculated about how visitor is picked up (7)

indicatorNotes.picked up: what is picked up is heard, so the answer is how the word is heard

blocks.note: a visitor is a guest, and that word said aloud is a past-tense verb spelt differently

annotation.surface: Someone wonders how a caller might be collected from the station.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as fetching a visitor by car; it means heard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: forming an opinion without firm evidence.

entries.clue: Music system created by some austere orchestras (6)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters of the phrase are used

blocks.note: drop AU from the front and keep only the O of the second word

annotation.surface: A sound system is designed by a few severe orchestras.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words: the end of 'austere' plus the O of 'orchestras'.
annotation.definitionFit: A stereo is a two-channel system for playing music.

entries.clue: Cheers advanced facility (6)

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers
to advance money is to lend it

annotation.surface: A pub toast, followed by a new state-of-the-art building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facility' looks like a building; it is the other sense, a knack. Ta and cheers are both casual British thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of natural ability: a facility with numbers is a gift for them.

entries.clue: Way to seek admission that will sound familiar (4,1,4)

annotation.definitionNote: the first definition is a noun phrase; ring a bell is the action it names

blocks.note: you ring the doorbell to be let in
a name that rings a bell is one you seem to know

annotation.surface: A tip on how to get into a house that the reader will half recognise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is a nudge toward the bell itself, which makes the two senses meet neatly.
annotation.definitionFit: Ringing the bell is how you ask to come in; something that rings a bell sounds familiar.

entries.clue: Published fiction on queen is something abnormal (7)

blocks.note: a book that is out has been published

annotation.surface: A newly released novel about a queen is judged strange.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Published fiction' reads as one thing, a novel, but it splits in two. Queen as R is from the Latin regina.
annotation.definitionFit: An outlier is a data point or thing far from the norm.

entries.clue: Mostly what you wear and feel in battle (6,7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a verb phrase; the answer is the condition felt

indicatorNotes.Mostly: most of the phrase is kept: the last letter goes

blocks.note: the camouflage uniform soldiers wear, a plural name

annotation.surface: A description of the soldier's uniform and the strain felt in war.
annotation.walkthrough: The clothing and the condition share a name, one letter apart.
annotation.definitionFit: Combat fatigue is the exhaustion and stress soldiers suffer in battle.

entries.clue: Promote extremely punctual underling (4)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take only the extremes, the first and last letters, of each word

annotation.surface: A boss rewards a very reliable junior with a promotion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely punctual' reads as very punctual; 'extremely' covers both words that follow.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: an author on a chat show mentions a new book to push sales.

entries.clue: Texan lopes about finding places out of this world (10)

indicatorNotes.about: the letters are moved about into a new order

annotation.surface: A cowboy ambles around and stumbles on somewhere otherworldly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of this world' usually means wonderful; here it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Exoplanets are planets outside our solar system.

entries.clue: Casually called wife the most beautiful in America (6)

blocks.note: the beauty-contest winner holds the title Miss

annotation.surface: A husband calls his wife the loveliest woman in America.
annotation.walkthrough: Miss US would be the country's beauty queen. Missus is informal British for wife.
annotation.definitionFit: The missus is a casual word for one's wife.

entries.clue: Biblical fellow creating difficulty in African country (8)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece goes in the other

annotation.surface: A man from the Bible stirs up trouble on a trip to Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Creating' only links; Benin is the small West African country beside Nigeria, and the difficulty goes inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Benjamin was Jacob's youngest son in Genesis.

entries.clue: Sad fitter abandoned initial romantic encounter (5,4)

indicatorNotes.abandoned: abandoned as in wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

annotation.surface: A gloomy tradesman walked out of a first romantic meeting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as walking out on the date; it signals letters without restraint.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: initial matches the ordinal, and a romantic encounter arranged in advance is a date.

entries.clue: Being in good form accurately underpins race odds (9)

indicatorNotes.underpins: in a down answer, what underpins goes below

blocks.note: SP = starting price, the odds at the off

annotation.surface: A racing tipster whose accurate form reading supports the odds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good form' sounds like racing form, the horse's record; it means lively. SP is the betting term for the starting price.
annotation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and full of energy.

entries.clue: You express absolute resolution when starting this time (4)

indicatorNotes.when starting: take each word at its start, its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

annotation.surface: New Year talk: this time I mean it, says the resolution-maker.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a New Year's resolution, and the answer is the year it starts.
annotation.definitionFit: The year is the period the resolution is meant to cover.

entries.clue: Fossil fuel that may lead to war? (4)

blocks.note: peat, cut in blocks from bogs and burnt on the fire
a word that goes before 'war' for a fight between gangs over territory

annotation.surface: A remark that burning fossil fuels might end in conflict.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is a word that comes before 'war': a turf war. Turf is peat, the fuel dug from bogs in Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: Turf is peat for burning, and it goes before 'war' in turf war.

entries.clue: Wedges have this fine finish – it’s just the start (4,3)

blocks.note: a wedge tapers to a narrow edge at one end
from the idiom for a small first step that will lead to much worse

annotation.surface: A remark about wedges' neat edge, plus a warning of more to come.
annotation.walkthrough: The idiom 'the thin end of the wedge' names a small first step toward something bigger.
annotation.definitionFit: A wedge ends thinly, and the thin end of the wedge is only the start.

entries.clue: Unrivalled competition? Not so much (9)

annotation.surface: Someone asks if the rivalry is unbeatable and is told: not really.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unrivalled competition' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'Unrivalled'.
annotation.definitionFit: Matchless means without equal.

entries.clue: Reluctantly deliver expression of horror to disrupt power grab (5,2)

indicatorNotes.to disrupt: the word breaks into the other and splits it

annotation.surface: A reluctant messenger's cry of dismay helps foil an attempted takeover.
annotation.walkthrough: UGH breaks COUP into CO and UP.
annotation.definitionFit: To cough up is to hand over money or information unwillingly.

entries.clue: Devotee of major pop sensation broke wifi set (7)

indicatorNotes.broke: broken letters are reassembled in a new order

annotation.surface: An excited fan of a big pop star crashes the wifi setup.
annotation.walkthrough: The pop sensation is Taylor Swift, whose fans are called Swifties.
annotation.definitionFit: A Swiftie is a devoted fan of Taylor Swift.

entries.clue: Boiled rice in iron container – that’s very intense (6)

indicatorNotes.Boiled: boiled letters are stirred into a new order
indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters go in the other piece

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

annotation.surface: Rice boiled in an iron pot turns out scorching hot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Container' is part of the kitchen picture; the pot that holds the rice is FE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: heat, competition or loyalty described this way is at full strength.

entries.clue: Fish sounding very small to contribute food for Italians (8)

indicatorNotes.sounding: the answer is how the words sound when spoken

blocks.note: the ling is a sea fish
weeny = tiny; run on after the fish, it gives the rest of the sound

annotation.surface: A tiny fish plays its part in an Italian meal.
annotation.walkthrough: LING + WEENY, said together, gives the pasta's sound.
annotation.definitionFit: Linguini is a flat Italian pasta.

entries.clue: Media snubs insider’s return – it’s not reported (6)

indicatorNotes.insider’s: the answer is inside the words

annotation.surface: The press ignores a whistleblower's comeback, so the story goes untold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Insider' reads as a whistleblower; it points to letters inside the words.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: something left unspoken has not been told to anyone.

entries.clue: Informed about liberal jargon (5)

indicatorNotes.about: one piece goes about, around, the other

blocks.note: an informer sings to the police

annotation.surface: Someone told on a liberal over their use of jargon.
annotation.walkthrough: To sing is underworld slang for informing, so the past tense SANG = informed.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: both name the vocabulary a particular group uses in place of standard words.

entries.clue: Don’t be fooled by this flimsy type of material (3,7)

blocks.note: to detect a trick or a liar's real motive
sheer fabric, thin enough to show what is behind it

annotation.surface: A warning not to be taken in by a cheap, thin fabric.
annotation.walkthrough: The verb phrase and the adjective are spelt alike.
annotation.definitionFit: You see through a deception; sheer fabric is see-through.

entries.clue: Pretentious faction loses power (4)

indicatorNotes.loses: a group that loses something no longer has it, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a political party is a faction

annotation.surface: A political splinter group, full of airs, is voted out of office.
annotation.walkthrough: PARTY without its P.
annotation.definitionFit: Arty means showily artistic, pretentious.

entries.clue: Really dull study of poet (6)

blocks.note: dry = very dull, as in dry as dust
a den is a study, a private room

annotation.surface: A critic calls an academic study of a poet deadly boring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Study' reads as a piece of scholarship; it is the room. John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet.
annotation.definitionFit: John Dryden was England's first Poet Laureate.

entries.clue: Top primate nursing bruised ego (6)

indicatorNotes.nursing: to nurse is to hold, so APE holds the other letters
indicatorNotes.bruised: bruised letters are knocked into a new order

annotation.surface: The alpha ape comforts a rival whose pride has been hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top primate' reads as the alpha ape; 'Top' is the definition alone.
annotation.definitionFit: An apogee is the highest point, a peak.
